title: Numbers & Operations
description: Class 4 IMO — Numbers & Operations: 5- and 6-digit numbers, place value in the Indian system (lakhs), rounding, and addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of large numbers.

topics.title: 5- and 6-digit Numbers & Place Value
topics.concept:
In the Indian system, after the Hundreds, Tens and Ones come Thousands, Ten Thousands and Lakhs. A 6-digit number such as 4,52,310 has 4 Lakhs, 5 Ten Thousands, 2 Thousands, 3 Hundreds, 1 Ten and 0 Ones.

The smallest 6-digit number is 1,00,000 (one lakh) and the largest is 9,99,999. The place of a digit gives its value, so the 5 in 4,52,310 stands for 50,000.

examples.problem: What is the place value of 5 in 4,52,310?
examples.solution: 5 is in the Ten Thousands place, so its value is 50,000.

examples.problem: Write the smallest and largest 6-digit numbers.

recap: Indian places: Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Ten Thousands, Lakhs.

quiz.q: What is the place value of 7 in 7,30,425?
quiz.explanation: 7 is in the Lakhs place, so its value is 7,00,000.

topics.title: Rounding & Adding/Subtracting Large Numbers
topics.concept:
To round a number, look at the digit just after the place you are rounding to. If it is 5 or more, round up; otherwise round down. So 4,567 rounded to the nearest 1000 is 5,000.

Large numbers are added and subtracted column by column, carrying or borrowing exactly as with smaller numbers.

examples.solution: The hundreds digit 5 is 5 or more, so it rounds up to 5,000.

recap: Round up if the next digit is 5 or more, else round down.
Add and subtract large numbers column by column.

quiz.explanation: The tens digit 8 is 5 or more, so it rounds up to 3,500.

topics.title: Multiplication & Division of Large Numbers
topics.concept:
To multiply a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number, multiply by the ones and the tens separately, then add. For 234 × 12: 234 × 2 = 468 and 234 × 10 = 2,340, so 468 + 2,340 = 2,808.

To divide, share place by place from the left. For 4,824 ÷ 6 = 804, and we can check with 804 × 6 = 4,824.
recap: Multiply by ones and tens separately, then add.

questions.q: In 3,45,678, which digit is in the Lakhs place?
questions.explanation: The leftmost digit 3 is in the Lakhs place.
The hundreds digit 7 is 5 or more, so it rounds up to 7,000.
90,000 is greater than all the others.

questions.q: What is the place value of 6 in 6,54,321?
questions.explanation: 6 is in the Lakhs place, so its value is 6,00,000.
